proofs.full_local_argument: Fix N>=1, T>=1, 0<beta<1, any realized binary expert-prediction/label sequence, and expert i. Let k_i count trials on which both WM and expert i err. The selected updates give w_i,fin=beta^k_i. Since k_i<=m_i and beta<1, w_i,fin>=beta^m_i, hence W_fin>=beta^m_i>0. On a WM mistake let q_wrong be the weight predicting its wrong label and q_right the remaining weight. Weighted majority, including either tie choice, gives q_wrong>=q_right, hence q_wrong>=W/2. Thus W_new=beta*q_wrong+q_right=W-(1-beta)*q_wrong<=((1+beta)/2)*W. On a correct WM prediction all weights are unchanged. Starting with W_init=N, induction gives W_fin<=N*((1+beta)/2)^M. Combining yields beta^m_i<=N*((1+beta)/2)^M. Taking natural logarithms and rearranging gives M*ln(2/(1+beta))<=ln N+m_i*ln(1/beta). Since 0<beta<1 makes the denominator positive, division proves the claim for every i. The argument holds for each realized sequence, including adaptive histories, without distributional or independence assumptions.

assumptions: All pool predictions are available before the master predicts; the binary label is revealed afterwards.
Initial weights are all one; one fixed beta satisfies 0<beta<1.
No stochastic, realizability or best-expert mistake-budget assumption is needed.
statement.conclusion: For every i, M <= (ln N + m_i*ln(1/beta))/ln(2/(1+beta)). Therefore the same bound holds with min_i m_i. There are no unspecified constants.
statement.objects_and_definitions: N binary pool predictors, T trials, labels y_t in {0,1}, predictions a_i,t in {0,1}. WM starts with w_i=1, predicts a weighted-majority label with arbitrary fixed deterministic tie-breaking, and multiplies incorrect experts' weights by beta only when WM errs. M=sum_t 1{WM_t!=y_t}; m_i=sum_t 1{a_i,t!=y_t}.
statement.parameter_domains: N,T positive integers; beta real in (0,1); M,m_i integers in [0,T]. Logarithms below are natural.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer N>=1, finite integer T>=1, fixed beta in (0,1), every realized binary prediction/label sequence compatible with the protocol, and each i=1,...,N, the inequality holds pathwise. No expectation or success probability.
